page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2d server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, operating with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, which ensures no hyperthreading resource sharing. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In terms of performance, the t2d-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU capabilities, ranking in the top 25% of benchmarks with a stress-ng single-core score of 2688.09. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the average range, scoring 21511.57 in stress-ng. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average performance, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 996.35 GB/sec, and uncached large block read and write speeds measuring 95.12 GB/sec and 51.75 GB/sec, respectively. Other standard benchmarks, such as Geekbench (1455.0 single-core, 7817.0 multi-core) and Passmark CPU (16769.54), consistently align with mid-tier performance expectations.

This hardware profile is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations. The instance achieved a static web serving throughput of 11.61 GB/sec and a Passmark database operations score of 6859.59. It can also handle lightweight machine learning tasks, demonstrating an LLM inference speed of 15.0 tokens/sec for text generation on a medium 7B model. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation provides predictable performance without the resource contention of shared-core models, though the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators limits its applicability for high-performance storage-heavy databases or intensive deep learning training.
